voyage.name: Peristylium
voyage.content: Main square of Diocletian's palace with well preserved Roman architecture.

voyage.name: Katedrala sv. Duje
voyage.content: Built around 305 AD as a mausoleum of Roman emperor Diocletian's (the oldest cathedral building in the world). The cathedral is also a very beautiful mixture of Roman temple and Catholic church. It also has a beautiful belltower which provides you a great panoramic view of Split, nearby islands and Marjan hill.

voyage.name: St. Duje's bell tower
voyage.content: Beautiful belltower which provides you a great panoramic view of Split, nearby islands and Marjan hill. The ascent is certainly not for those with vertigo, but the views from the top are marvelous. It costs €1.40 to go up the bell tower.

voyage.name: Jupiter temple
voyage.content: Ancient Roman temple which became St. John's church.

voyage.name: Getski vrtal
voyage.content: It is the smallest park in Split, situated in the Diocletian's palace at the Dominisova street (Marko Antonio De Dominis street). In that park are beautiful traditional Dalmatian tiramolas. During the summer these are full of clothes drying in the sunshine. In every guidebook about Split you have pictures from the Getski vrtal. It is the location of a 500-year-old stone house which was destroyed during World War II.

voyage.name: Basement halls of Diocletian's Palace
voyage.content: Exceptionally well preserved substructure of Diocletian's Palace now open as a museum. One of the locations in Game of Thrones. It's strongly recommended to book a tour guide, otherwise visitors walk through mostly empty halls with barely further information.

voyage.name: Galerija Meštrović
voyage.content: The gallery contains works of Ivan Meštrović, famous Croatian sculptor.

voyage.name: Archaeological Museum
voyage.content: The oldest museum in Croatia (1820), about 20 min walk north of the old town. Many artifacts and monuments from Roman colonies Salona and Narona. Most of the panel information is only in Croatian, so use a translator app or bring a Croatian friend.

voyage.name: Old graveyards
voyage.content: Sustipan and old Jewish cemetery

voyage.name: Froggyland
voyage.content: A strange museum for 21 dioramas of taxidermy frogs in a variety of everyday human situations, crafted in the early 1900s.

voyage.name: Split city beach
voyage.content: If you have a longer stop-over in Split, 5 min south of the passenger terminal and the train and bus stations lies Split's city beach where you can take a plunge in the Adriatic.

voyage.name: Picigin
voyage.content: Traditional beach game with a small ball (Bačvice beach). In summer every year there is a world championship in picigin.

voyage.name: Grgur Ninski
voyage.content: It is said that if you touch the big toe of the statue and make a wish your wish will come true.

voyage.name: HNK Hajduk Split
voyage.content: They play in Prva HNL, the top tier of football in Croatia; indeed they've never been out of it, and have won it several times. Their home ground of Poljud stadium (capacity 34,000) is 1 km north of the main bus station, harbour and old city. Don't go for the cheapest seats as these are in the north stand, the Torcida bastion of home fanatics.

voyage.name: Beach at Bačvice
voyage.content: This beach has beautiful fine-grained sand, and it is very shallow. There are many cafes and places to eat ice cream. It is certainly not the best beach in Croatia (it is packed solid most of summer), but it will give you a feeling of 'real' Croatia as the vast majority of people who go there are from Split. You can also play Picigin here. To reach this beach, walk South along the waterfront from the bus station and

voyage.name: Pazar
voyage.content: Farmers market with perfect fruit, vegetables and more. The best time to visit the market is Saturday or Sunday morning.

voyage.name: Ribarnica
voyage.content: Fresh fish market.

voyage.name: Marmontova
voyage.content: Shopping street in the centre.

voyage.name: City Center One
voyage.content: Opened in 2010. 3 floors (5 garage levels) and Cineplexx cinema.

voyage.name: Mall of Split
voyage.content: Opened in 2016.

voyage.name: Pizza Cut Planet 1
voyage.content: A good offer for those who want to try several types of pizzas without buying them completely. Great pizza idea. Several flavours to choose from.

voyage.name: Vege
voyage.content: Delicious and fresh vegan food. The best veggies in Split. Good atmosphere and homemade food made live.

voyage.name: Sandwich Bar Rizzo
voyage.content: The best sandwiches in Split. Always fresh food and very helpful staff.

voyage.name: Ba!Će
voyage.content: Balkan atmosphere. Ba!Cevapi is their flagship dish, which consists of minced meat, well spiced and grilled, served with typical bread and sauces

voyage.name: Pizzeria Kaleta
voyage.content: Freshly baked dough, crispy just as it should be, chicken and hearty side dishes. Great pizza

voyage.name: Zlatna ribica
voyage.content: Great local spot for delicious seafood. Friendly staff. Not many tables so you may have to wait for an available table.

voyage.name: Theatrum Bar & Food
voyage.content: Reservation can be made via email, phone or social media. Dine in, curbside-pickup, delivery, seating, Wi-Fi, fresh ingredients, breakfast, dinner, lunch.

voyage.name: Fino i Friško 2 - Biškić
voyage.content: Because of its proximity to school, this bakery always has fresh and tasty food.

voyage.name: Fife
voyage.content: Lively and busy restaurant with lots of seating and deliciously large Croatian dishes.

voyage.name: Popaj
voyage.hours: Mon-Thu winter 08:00-00:00, summer 08:00-01:00, Fri Sat winter 08:00-13:00, summer 08:00-14:00, Sun winter 15:00-00:00, summer 15:00-01:00
voyage.content: The most popular fast food in Split with great pizzeta (small pizza, €2) and very big ham sandwich (€2.70).

voyage.name: Kod Joze
voyage.content: The traditional family-run konoba serves tasty dishes in style. Prices very reasonable considering the quality and atmosphere.

voyage.name: Bakra - Steak & Pizza Bar
voyage.content: Definitely one of the best pizza in town, baked on fireplace.

voyage.name: Biser Orijenta
voyage.content: Good "European Chinese" cuisine. Not too popular among the locals, but the prices are fair and the service is friendly.

voyage.name: Konoba Marjan
voyage.content: Risottos, pasticada (marinaded veal cooked in sauce), and excellent fish. Prices are very reasonable and the staff very friendly. English spoken.

voyage.name: Kod Sfinge Vanevropske Zviri
voyage.content: A Konoba/Trattoria. Good Dalmatian specialties: Pašticada, Paški sir, etc. Also proposes good seafood catch of the day, but sometimes unavailable. Seems to be operated by a single family: The waiters knows very well the menu!

voyage.name: Konoba Insula
voyage.content: Small side street restaurant run by a young married couple, incredible food at a very fair price.

voyage.name: Nostromo
voyage.content: Good seafood and salad in a rather smoky ambience with friendly service.

voyage.name: St Riva
voyage.content: Has an upper story that overlooks the promenade.

voyage.name: Sanctuary Bar
voyage.content: The beachhead of craft cocktails in Split, with a selection of craft beers as well. Run by US expat, Tristan.

voyage.name: Gaga Bar
voyage.content: Cosy atmosphere, long list of cocktails, Latin music. Ask for a bill, because one round is €14, and then second one (the same one) may be €20. Atmosphere is nice, but the waiters are not. More tourists than locals.

voyage.name: Vanilla Club
voyage.content: Fancy place by the swimming pool with popular domestic and foreign music.

voyage.name: Hostel Split Backpackers 2
voyage.content: Lively hostel popular with solo travelers. Well located between the old town and the bus and train stations. Dorm from €15.

voyage.name: Tchaikovsky Hostel
voyage.content: Chill hostel with only few guests around during low-season. Shared kitchen. Wifi.

voyage.name: Al's Place
voyage.content: Hostel open Easter to Oct run by British expat Al. The hostel is in an 800-year-old stone house inside the city walls, small and cozy with only 12 beds in 2 en suite rooms. There is also kitchen and common area, A/C, and laundry.

voyage.name: CroParadise Green Hostel
voyage.content: Has several units scattered across Old Town, lacks communal area for socialising. LCD televisions and computers with free internet access, some rooms dingy and noisy.

voyage.name: Old Town Hostel
voyage.content: Free wifi, one shared computer, flat screen TV with a collection of movies.

voyage.name: Hostel Split
voyage.content: Very central, between bus station and old town. With 8-bedded dorm and private rooms.

voyage.name: Adriatic Hostel
voyage.content: Newly renovated with chandeliers, hardwood floors, modern bathrooms with custom glass showers (hotel style), A/C and flatscreen TVs in every room, stainless steel appliances in gourmet kitchen, new bedding and towels, huge lounge where guests can rest and chat, laundry room, internet stations.

voyage.name: Guesthouse Vrlic
voyage.content: Small central place.

voyage.name: Villa Varoš
voyage.content: Clean comfy small hotel, very central, friendly helpful hosts.

voyage.name: Hotel Atrium
voyage.content: Modern hotel in business district, with 124 rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Mondo
voyage.content: Business hotel in an industrial part of town, free parking.

voyage.name: Hotel Globo
voyage.content: Workaday neighbourhood but hotel is clean & well-run, close to central sights.

voyage.name: Hotel Luxe
voyage.content: Decent place in town centre, some street noise, some rooms are in Annex 500 m away.

voyage.name: Hotel Park
voyage.content: Good central hotel, claims to be 5 star but it's more like 3 or 4, and the room rates are in line with that.

voyage.name: Hotel Peristil
voyage.content: Friendly small place within the old palace.

voyage.name: Hotel Vestibul Palace
voyage.content: Within the old palace, so some rooms are small and you'll regret trying to bring a car, but excellent service and a comfy modern place in the centre.

voyage.name: Marmont
voyage.content: Central in old town, most rooms are small and dark, and parking is difficult. But it's clean and simple and has A/C.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Resort & Spa, Split
voyage.content: Bland modern building, but a well-run resort hotel with beach club and good grill restaurant. With spa, but the indoor pool is closed indefinitely for repairs. One repeat visitor was impressed by the low staff turnover.

voyage.name: Riva Apartments
voyage.content: Self-catering apartments on Riva promenade looking out to Split Bay.

voyage.name: Palace Suites Heritage Hotel
voyage.content: Suites overlooking the main square, locally known as the Pjaca.

voyage.name: Hotel POSH
voyage.content: All-suites, 5* hotel with an amazing sea view, infinity pool, and Vip service.

voyage.name: Adria Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm bed: €15-25; bed in private room: €18-28
voyage.content: Right next to the Adriatic Sea.

voyage.name: Hotel San Antonio
voyage.content: 54 rooms and 3 suites.
